title: Pharmacy
summary: Pharmacists can give advice on common illnesses, minor health concerns and medicines questions. If they cannot help, they can refer you to a GP or another healthcare professional.
suitableFor: Pharmacy First common conditions where clinically appropriate
Advice on whether another service may be needed
notSuitableFor: Situations where you are unsure and need urgent medical guidance
safetyNote: If you are unsure where to get help, use NHS 111.

title: GP or Student Health Service
summary: A GP can help with non-urgent health concerns, ongoing symptoms, prescriptions, referrals and follow-up care. University of Bristol students may be able to register with the Students' Health Service if they are in the practice area.
suitableFor: Registering with a GP as a student
notSuitableFor: Situations where you need urgent advice now and cannot wait for an appointment
safetyNote: If you need medical help now but it is not life-threatening, use NHS 111.
sourceLabel: University of Bristol Students' Health Service

title: NHS 111
summary: NHS 111 can help when you think you need medical help now but it is not a life-threatening emergency. It can direct you to the right service.
suitableFor: You need medical help now but it is not an emergency
You are not sure which NHS service to use
You need urgent advice when your GP is closed
safetyNote: If you or someone else is in immediate danger, call 999.

title: 999 or A&E
summary: 999 and A&E are for life-threatening emergencies, serious injuries, or situations where someone may be in immediate danger.
suitableFor: You think urgent emergency care is needed
safetyNote: Call 999 immediately if there is a life-threatening emergency.
